statement: Ulysses is strongest as a calm editor, library, and export environment.
Scrivener is strongest as a project container with binder, research adjacency, and compile control.
iA Writer treats the editor as an instrument and emphasizes syntax, style, and provenance-oriented writing behavior.
Drafts is strongest at text-first capture, routing, and automation.
Graph functionality is better treated as a projection than as the primary manuscript store or writing surface.
The recommended durable substrate combines local manuscript files, structured metadata, manifests, compile profiles, patch/session history, and a rebuildable catalog.
SQLite is recommended for the working catalog, with full-text search first and graph/semantic systems later.
AI changes should enter as inspectable patches rather than invisible source mutation.
The manuscript should remain the primary product while Compendium and worldbuilding systems remain subordinate.
Compile and export should be first-class deterministic operations with visible warnings and traceability.
Manifest-first, file-owned canonical state resolves the tension between portability and fast application behavior.
Object, placement, revision, and anchor identities must remain distinct to support reuse, patching, evidence, restore, and source maps.
PatchSession and Recovery require a shared Mutation Envelope to avoid competing transaction models.
Cursor, scroll, panes, and recent context are local user state rather than canonical manuscript metadata.
The stress assay should shape architecture early rather than appear after specifications are complete.
